text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:

- An exchange of letters on Tuesday between Swiss Minister Jean-Pascal Delamuraz and World Jewish Congress President Edgar Bronfman allows cooperation on searching for funds of Holocaust victims to continue. Delamuraz apologised for a statement he made that offended many. Political parties, banks and Jewish communities reacted positively.
- Between 150 and 180 people will lose their jobs after the merger of Helvetia Insurance and Artisana Insurance into Helsana Versicherungen AG.
- Swiss property and real estate prices continue to fall, with apartment rents falling the most.
- Von Roll and von Moos have not yet reached an agreement on the cost of taking over the steel works in Gerlafingen.
- The new furnace at the von Moos Holding steel works in Gerlafingen is emitting a high level of harmful substances into the atmosphere, forcing Von Moos to reduce production.
- The PTT will increase fees for using its payment system by nearly 10 percent starting February 1.
- UBS deputy director and historian Erwin Haggenmueller, who is head of the bank's historical archive, broke the law when he ordered the shredding of documents.
- The number of bankruptcies filed in 1996 rose by 4.4 percent to 10,192.
